jp-pole-plates.reliability: Strong regional clue when the plate style is clearly visible and matched to the correct utility region.
jp-pole-plates.howToUse: Use the plate as regional evidence, then confirm with other pole hardware, road context, and landscape.
jp-pole-plates.exceptions: Plate style and visibility vary. Do not infer a region from a tiny or unclear plate.
jp-pole-plates.falseFriends: Other pole labels and nationwide hardware can look superficially similar.
jp-pole-plates.reviewNote: Seed entry based on the linked current country guide. Production review should attach example locations and reviewer history.

jp-reflectors.reliability: Useful regional evidence when the reflector design is visible clearly.
jp-reflectors.howToUse: Compare shape, color, placement, and the rest of the pole rather than treating any reflector as a lock.
jp-reflectors.exceptions: Generic reflector patterns also occur, so regional value depends on the specific design.
jp-reflectors.falseFriends: Taiwan and South Korea can produce similar high-level utility-pole impressions.
jp-reflectors.reviewNote: Seed entry; visual examples are intentionally left open for reviewed community additions.

jp-kei.reliability: Strong supporting national context when a kei-car plate is clearly visible.
jp-kei.howToUse: Treat the plate color as one part of the wider Japanese road and vehicle environment.
jp-kei.exceptions: Blur, lighting, and distance can distort plate color.
jp-kei.falseFriends: Do not use a yellow-looking blur as a standalone country lock.

gh-tape.reliability: Very strong where the known taped roof-rack feature is clearly visible.
gh-tape.howToUse: Confirm that the visible feature is the correct roof-rack/tape configuration rather than a random dark shape.
gh-tape.exceptions: The clue is not present on every Ghana round and coverage generations differ.
gh-tape.falseFriends: Absence of the tape does not rule Ghana out.

gh-gen4.reliability: Strong supporting clue when the pickup/antenna appearance matches the documented coverage.
gh-gen4.howToUse: Use the vehicle clue together with Ghanaian road and landscape context.
gh-gen4.exceptions: Vehicle visibility and blur vary between panoramas.
gh-gen4.falseFriends: Antennas and vehicle edges also occur in other countries, so match the whole appearance.
gh-gen4.reviewNote: Seed entry based on the linked source guide.

co-yellow.reliability: Very strong national clue in South America when plate color is clearly visible.
co-yellow.howToUse: Check multiple vehicles when possible and combine with Colombian road, terrain, and sign context.
co-yellow.exceptions: Distance, blur, glare, and unusual vehicles can make plate color unreliable.
co-yellow.falseFriends: Do not identify Colombia from any yellow rectangle without confirming it is a licence plate.

co-cross.reliability: Strong supporting clue when the white metal signpost-back construction is clearly visible.
co-cross.howToUse: Inspect the rear construction of the sign and pair it with Colombian plate and road context.
co-cross.exceptions: Similar white posts can occur elsewhere.
co-cross.falseFriends: The useful feature is the construction pattern, not simply a white signpost.

gt-car.reliability: Very strong when the grey car, roof rack, and side mirrors are visible in the expected configuration.
gt-car.howToUse: Check the full visible-car pattern, then use language, driving side, architecture, and terrain as confirmation.
gt-car.exceptions: Visibility changes by panorama and not every scene presents the car equally clearly.
gt-car.falseFriends: Other visible-car coverages can look similar at a glance.

gt-architecture.reliability: Moderate. Best treated as part of a visual combination rather than a standalone clue.
gt-architecture.howToUse: Combine building materials and colors with terrain, road quality, language, and the Google car.
gt-architecture.exceptions: Similar construction appears across Central America and other tropical regions.
gt-architecture.falseFriends: Architecture alone should rarely be a country lock.

tw-poles.reliability: Moderate in this seed version; exact regional claims require stronger example coverage.
tw-poles.howToUse: Study labels and pole hardware as a family, then confirm with road prefixes, area codes, terrain, and settlement context.
tw-poles.exceptions: Regional utility infrastructure is complex and should not be generalized from a small sample.
tw-poles.falseFriends: Japan and South Korea can share a similar high-level pole-and-wires texture.
